meta.title: Snug: Bookmark export, import and backup
meta.description: Export, import and back up your bookmarks in common formats, from Chrome or Safari, on a schedule. Everything stays local.

hero.subheadline: Snug exports, imports and backs up your bookmarks in Chrome and other Chromium browsers. It makes no network calls and needs no account.
hero.note: Free. Open source. Works in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera.

trust.heading: An extension that has no server to trust
trust.intro: Snug reads and writes your browser's own bookmarks tree, on your device. It never connects to anything, so there is nowhere for your bookmarks to go.

network.title: No network calls
network.body: Snug makes none. Every export and import happens locally.

account.title: No account
account.body: There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to log in to.

source.title: Open source
source.body: The code is public. Read it, or check the project's OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges, CodeQL scans and CI runs.

trust.access: Reading and writing your bookmarks is the only way an extension can export and import them. Snug does that and nothing else.

proof.heading: What people say
proof.numbers: 5,000 users. 4.8 stars from 20 ratings on the Chrome Web Store (2026-10-05).
proof.renameNote: These are public Chrome Web Store reviews. Most were written before Snug was renamed, when the listing was called "Bookmark Import/Export", so they describe the export and import, not the current interface.
proof.link: Read all reviews on the Chrome Web Store

network.question: Does Snug send my bookmarks anywhere?
network.answer: No. Snug makes no network calls. It reads and writes your browser's bookmarks on your device, and the source code is public so you can check.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. Install it and start exporting.

sync.question: Does it sync my bookmarks between devices?
sync.answer: No. Snug has no sync and no cloud. To move bookmarks to another browser or computer, export a file and import it there.

oneFile.question: Can I import several files at once?
oneFile.answer: No. Snug imports one file at a time. To bring in more than one, import them one after another.

permissions.question: Why does it need access to all my bookmarks?
permissions.answer: Reading and writing them is the only way an extension can export and import them. Snug makes no network calls, so nothing it reads can leave your device.

builtin.question: My browser already exports HTML. Why use Snug?
builtin.answer: The built-in export has no folder selection, preview, undo, schedule, duplicate check or extra formats. Snug has all of them.

overwrite.question: Will it overwrite my current bookmarks?
overwrite.answer: Only if you choose Replace. You see a preview first, and Replace saves a Safety snapshot you can restore.

formats.question: Which formats does it handle?
formats.answer: Export as HTML, JSON, CSV, Markdown, OPML or XBEL. Import HTML, JSON, CSV or XBEL, a Chrome profile `Bookmarks` file, or a Safari export.

browsers.question: Which browsers does it work in?
browsers.answer: Chrome and other Chromium browsers such as Edge, Brave and Opera.

safe.question: Is it safe to install a solo developer's extension?
safe.answer: The source is public, CodeQL scans it, the project has OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges, and CI runs pinned. Judge it yourself on GitHub.

final.heading: Take your bookmarks with you
final.line: Add Snug to Chrome and export, import or back up in a few clicks. Free, open source, and nothing leaves your device.

footer.note: Snug is open source under the MIT license.
